findings.reason: Confirmed (high: a false item statement). Item symmetric-power-polarization asserts that Sym^{n−1} of any two-dimensional representation preserving an alternating form with multiplier μ takes values in G_n(F), with no restriction on n or on the characteristic, and G_n needs a nondegenerate form. I recomputed the red team's example exactly over F_7: for SL_2(F_7) acting on Sym^7 of its standard representation (n = 8), the U- and L-invariance equations have a one-dimensional solution space, spanned by B(v_i, v_{7−i}) = −i for 1 ≤ i ≤ 6 with v_i = x^{7−i}y^i. Its rank is 6, with radical span{x^7, y^7}. The same computation gives rank 5 on Sym^8 (n = 9). It gives nondegenerate forms in degrees 4, 5 and 6, which are p−3, p−2 and p−1 (n = p−2, p−1 and p), and also for p = 11 in degrees 9 and 10. Linear algebra commutes with field extension, so no nondegenerate invariant form exists over F̄_7 either. The paper uses the construction only for p > 5 and n ∈ {p−2, p−1} (proof of Theorem 2.1, published p. 513) and n = p (proof of Theorem 3.1, p. 516), where n−1 < p. So this is an overgeneralization by the extraction, not a source error. The fix is right: state the item for characteristic 0 or for odd p with n ≤ p, with nondegeneracy, the sign and the multiplier proved, and test degree p negatively.

Confirmed (high: a false item statement, printed in the source). The paper fixes the cohomological normalization: 'ρ̄_f is symplectic with multiplier ε̄^{1−k}' (published p. 513; arXiv v3 p. 5). On p. 516 (v3 p. 8) it prints ρ̄_f|I_p ≃ ω_2^{k−1} ⊕ ω_2^{p(k−1)}, and on p. 516 (v3 p. 9) it defines ω_2 as the reduction of the Lubin–Tate character ε_2 trivial on Art_{Q_{p^2}}(p). For any normalization of Art, the product of the two conjugate Lubin–Tate characters of Q_{p^2} restricts on inertia to the cyclotomic character, so ω_2^{p+1} = ε̄|I_p. The printed sum therefore has determinant ε̄^{k−1}|I_p, while det ρ̄_f = ε̄^{1−k}. These agree only if (p−1) | 2(k−1), which for 2 ≤ k < p means k = (p+1)/2; at p = 79 and k = 38 the exponents 37 and 41 differ mod 78. Item nonordinary-local-shape copies the printed formula, and none of E1–E8 records it. The conclusions that use it survive. Twist-invariance by ω_2^{(p^2−1)/2} is symmetric under a ↦ −a, so the dihedral exclusion still gives k ≡ (p+3)/2 mod (p+1). Likewise (m, p+1) = (k−1, p+1) for m = ±(k−1). The fix is right: use exponents 1−k and p(1−k), record a new sourceIssue, and leave the order and gcd conclusions unchanged.

Confirmed (high: a false item statement, printed in the source). Let φ be a lift of Art_{Q_p}(p). Then ε̄(φ) = 1, and since φ ∉ G_{Q_{p^2}}, the transfer gives φ² ≡ Art_{Q_{p^2}}(p), so ε_2(φ²) = 1. In the basis e, φe, Ind ε_2^{−m} has φ-matrix S = [0,1;1,0], of determinant −1. The irreducible ρ̄_f|G_{Q_p} has inertia ω_2^{a} ⊕ ω_2^{pa} (a = 1−k after /2), so it is Ind ω_2^{a} ⊗ λ for an unramified λ, and its determinant at φ, which must be ε̄^{1−k}(φ) = 1, is −λ(φ)². Hence λ(φ)² = −1. Then Sym^{p−1}ρ̄_f|G_{Q_p} ≅ ρ̄_{p,m} ⊗ λ^{p−1} with λ^{p−1}(φ) = (−1)^{(p−1)/2}. Only the middle monomial of Sym^{p−1} is fixed by the swap, so the traces of φ are 1 on ρ̄_{p,1} and (−1)^{(p−1)/2} on ρ̄|G_{Q_p}. For p ≡ 3 mod 4, including p = 79 (79 = 4·19 + 3), these are 1 and −1 = 78 in F_79, so ρ̄|G_{Q_p} ≇ ρ̄_{p,1} as printed (published p. 517, v3 p. 9). The extraction's note on local-shape-theorem-3-1 is right that the twist is quadratic when viewed on the level-2 inducing character: μ = λ|G_{Q_{p^2}} has μ(φ²) = −1. Its step 'which Sym^{p−1} kills (p − 1 is even)' is wrong, because on G_{Q_p} the twist λ has order 4. Item local-shape-theorem-3-1 and the component label in deformation-ring-nonordinary inherit the error. The fix is right. The twist η^{(p−1)/2} ⊗ ρ_{p,1} is crystalline of weight zero, its square is trivial so the GO_p multiplier is unchanged, and η is trivial on G_{F_v} ⊆ G_{Q_{p^2}} because p is inert in F^+. So the tensor-step identities on p. 517 are untouched, and the main theorem is not refuted.

Confirmed (high: a stage cycle). Route 2 (part-ii PolarizedAutomorphyLifting of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure) says that 'ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 and ML.3 … consume it'. It also imports 'Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions, ML.5) for cyclic base change and automorphic induction'. In data/atlas.json, ML.5 requires ML.3 and ML.4, and ML.3 requires ML.2, AN.4 and PA.5. I rebuilt the stage graph (stage requires, stageEdges and the 2318 links of the accepted restructurings projected to stages), and both ML.2 and ML.3 reach ML.5. So ML.3 → ML.5 → PolarizedAutomorphyLifting → ML.3 is a cycle as soon as the brief's import and its consumers are registered. ML.5's text ('Register cyclic base change, automorphic induction and selected tensor/symmetric-power transfers') is an endpoint registry, not an early supplier. The fix is right in direction. Remove the ML.5 import and take the soluble base change and automorphic induction behind [BLGGT14, Lems 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.4] from an early, source-scoped supplier upstream of the Part II, with ML.5 importing from it. Coordinate this with the confirmed RT-AREA-langlands-1/1, whose verdict asks for early Arthur–Clozel and unitary base-change inputs, and with the same defect reported in RT-PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/6. Recheck the expanded graph once the supplier is named.
